Alex: Heads-up — saw a 12% tail-latency regression on paged-attn after yesterday's kernel routing change. Traces point to more frequent kernel fallback for 512->1024 step transitions.
Maya: ugh, any repro? or just noisy in prod?
Alex: Repro on staging with the chat-batch workload. Reduced qps but same pattern. Attaching a small flame snippet.
perf-bot: Perf trace uploaded: https://perf.redwood/trace/1862345678 (flamegraph) :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Srinivas: Can you paste the kernel selection logs? want to see why fallback triggers — is it workspace size or new kernel missing fastpath for block size=256?
Alex: Log excerpt: ```KERNEL_SELECT model=redwood-tiny seq=1024 token_idx=512 candidate_kernels=[attn_fast_v2, attn_v1] selected=attn_v1 reason=workspace_shortage(estimated=420MB, avail=384MB)```
Tara: That looks like allocator fragmentation at the workspace boundary. We recently changed small-block reuse to be more aggressive which could increase fragmentation under mixed seq-lengths.
Jordan: Also note we added a conservative workspace estimate in the kernel router last week — might be overestimating required temp buffers.
Maya: If it falls back to attn_v1 that's slower and increases latency. Two levers: shrink workspace estimate or improve allocator packing to reduce fragmentation.
Srinivas: What about increasing block-size reuse thresholds? If we allow reusing blocks across different seq windows, compaction frequency might drop. But compaction cost could spike CPU/GPU sync.
Alex: Reuse candidate idea: reuse blocks only when last_used_ts within 200ms and sizes match ±16 bytes. That reduced fragmentation in a micro-run.
Maya: Do we have profiling showing compaction CPU time vs kernel fallback cost?
perf-bot: Quick numbers from staging (10k requests): ```fallbacks: +430, compactions: +12, compaction_time_total: 1.8s, avg_fallback_penalty: 28ms```
Jordan: So compaction is cheap compared to cumulative fallback penalty (430*28ms ≈ 12s). Means more aggressive compaction might be win.
Tara: But compaction can trigger device syncs if we naively memcpy/free. We need async reclaim path. Current drain path does: `free(block); cudaMemGetInfo()` — syncs.
Srinivas: Proposed plan: 1) add a non-blocking compaction path that enqueues async copy to a staging buffer then frees the old blocks on stream completion, 2) relax workspace estimator by 5% for attn_fast_v2, 3) tune block reuse TTL to 150-300ms and evaluate.
Maya: Sounds good. Can we try (1) and (3) quickly in a canary? which change is lowest risk?
Alex: (3) block reuse TTL tweak is lowest risk. I ran a quick canary with TTL=200ms + reuse loosened and saw fallbacks drop 60% and tail latency improved ~7%.
Jordan: Do we have the micro-benchmark commands to reproduce? paste here for others.
Alex: Repro script snippet: ```bash # run repro load ./bin/serve --model redwood-tiny --workspace=auto --blocksize=256 & ./tools/loadgen --qps=50 --seq=1024 --duration=120```
Tara: I'll prototype async compaction this morning. It needs careful stream ownership and hazard checks for KV cache pointers.
Srinivas: KV cache behavior: currently paged KV keeps page refs in a freelist which interacts with block reuse. If we reuse blocks too eagerly we may evict pages that are still referenced by in-flight requests. Need refcounts or epoch-based reclamation.
Maya: For immediate canary, we can keep refcounts but avoid epoch overhaul. Add atomic refcount bump on page pin and only consider blocks with refcount==0 for reuse. Cheap guard.
Jordan: Agree. Also add deterministic logging for kernel_selector to emit `est=420MB avail=384MB` so we can correlate with compaction events.
Alex: I'll open a PR for TTL change + kernel logging. Tara, sync with me on async compaction PR so we can coordinate tests.
Tara: Will do. I'll add metrics: compaction_count, compaction_sync_time, async_compaction_pending.
perf-bot: Test checklist template created: https://docs.redwood/testplans/paged-attn-compaction-1862345678 :white_check_mark:
Maya: Timeline? can we get a canary today and a broader staging run tomorrow?
Alex: TTL tweak + logging: canary in 2 hours. Async compaction prototype EOD. If staging results match, roll to prod next week with monitoring alerts.
Srinivas: One more: check kernel binary sizes — attn_fast_v2 allocates extra temp buffer when enabling fused kernels, maybe we can add an opt to share temp buffer across attention heads to cut estimate by ~10%. Worth exploring but medium risk.
Maya: Good call. Ok team — prioritize TTL canary and async compaction prototype. Keep messages in thread with numbers. Thanks :thumbsup:
